day_summary: SPCX ripped +7.7% on Day 3 of trading to close at $207.43, printing an intraday high of ~$211.75 (+10% from the $192.50 Day 2 close) before settling. Bloomberg ran the headline: SPCX is 'set for more than 50% jump in just three sessions' from the $135 IPO price — the final tally of $207.43 confirms it (+53.7%). The structural float mechanic that has driven every session is still fully in play: MSCI early-inclusion passive buying into a ~4% float with no meaningful short interest and no borrow. Today's session added a new layer: SPCX listed options began trading on Nasdaq for the first time, introducing the first hedging mechanism since the IPO. Initial IV is rich (estimated 80–90% front-week), spreads are wide, and bid-ask in the near-term options chain is uninvestable — but the options debut is a structural milestone that eventually unlocks institutional hedging and short-side discovery.

what_traders_are_doing: Allocants are trimming into Day 3 strength while holding a core for the index-inclusion runway. Disciplined new money is standing down — $207 is Day 3 of a record IPO at ~98x revenue, and the options market is not yet providing viable hedging infrastructure. Momentum desks rode the 10% intraday rip to $211.75 and took profits at the high; some rebuilt positions on the pullback to $205–$207 for a late-day hold. The debut of the options chain is drawing attention from volatility desks who are positioning as market makers and earning the wide spread. Near-consensus view: the float/passive-bid mechanic runs until MSCI demand exhausts (likely 2–4 more weeks), options spreads normalize in 3–5 sessions, and the first real entry with a protective put becomes viable at $190–200 on a pullback.

analysis:
## Day 3: +53.7% from the IPO offer, and options finally arrive

SPCX closed **$207.43** (+7.74%) on Day 3 of trading — [Bloomberg ran the headline](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-06-16/spacex-spcx-stock-set-for-more-than-50-jump-in-just-three-sessions) calling it 'set for more than 50% jump in just three sessions.' The final tally confirms it: from the $135 IPO price, the stock gained **+53.7% in three sessions**, pushing the fully-diluted market cap to approximately **$2.8T** per Bloomberg — roughly $100B above Amazon. The intraday high of **$211.75** (up 10% from the $192.50 Day 2 close) was the first meaningful rejection in three sessions, which is worth flagging.

## The options debut — a structural inflection

Today is not just Day 3 of a record IPO. [SPCX listed options began trading on Nasdaq for the first time](https://www.home.saxo/content/articles/options/options-brief--spacex-options-live-fomc-week--16-june-2026-16062026), resolving the final constraint flagged in the pre-IPO analysis: Wall Street had no mechanism to hedge or short SPCX. [CNBC noted before the IPO that 'there was no answer to the question of how to short SpaceX'](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/10/spacex-ipo-hedging-challenge-wall-street-short-nasa.html) — borrow was scarce, no put market existed. Today that changes. Front-week IV is estimated at 80–90% with wide bid-ask spreads (2–5 points on near-term strikes), which makes protective puts too expensive today for most approaches. But in 3–5 sessions as market makers build position, spreads compress, and the options chain becomes liquid — that is when a hedged entry at **$190–200** becomes the disciplined new-money setup.

## Still no chase — the discipline holds

The call remains **HOLD/WAIT at low conviction** for new money. Three sessions into a record IPO at **~98x revenue and ~$2.2T market cap**, buying $207 means paying the full passive-bid premium with no fundamental anchor until **~Sept 2 earnings**. The original $130–145 dip entry never came; the revised $190–205 pullback entry from the morning verdict was overrun before the open; the next actionable zone is **$190–200 on a pullback with a protective put** (viable once options spreads normalize). Allocants up ~$72/share from the IPO should be trimming into Day 3 strength and holding a reduced core. The float/passive-bid mechanic is real, powerful, and has 2–4 more weeks of runway — but it is a supply-and-demand phenomenon, not an earnings one, and **FOMC June 17** plus the ~December lock-up are the events that can turn a thin-float melt-up into a thin-float reversal.
